B.LEAGUE Play-by-Play

Source: R/bleague.R
bleague_pbp.Rd

Play-by-play of one finished B.LEAGUE game, in game order, every feed in one shape.

Endpoint: GET https://b-league.s3.amazonaws.com/web_json/v2_genius_contexts/{schedule_key}/{latest}.json (the v1 feed, or the game page's embed, when v2 does not hold the game).

One row per logged event, oldest first (event_no ascends; v2 counts in steps of 1000). action, qualifier2 and qualifier3 are English slugs for the numeric codes (NA for a code no sample contains); the team-rebound codes 18 / 19 mean opposite things on the two feeds and action follows the feed column. A v1 substitution is ONE row (action substitution, player_id out, player2_id in), a v2 one is two rows (player_out / player_in). home_score / away_score split the running score. x / y / area_code / success exist on v2 from 2022-23 and side from 2025-26 (see bleague_shots()). recorded_at / edited_at are UTC instants (POSIXct, tz UTC). Game-level rows (start, period, clock) carry NA team and player columns.

Usage

bleague_pbp(schedule_key, season = NULL)

Arguments

schedule_key

(integer required): B.LEAGUE ScheduleKey, one global sequence across B1, B2, B3 and every season, e.g. 504734 (B1 2025-26 sec 1, Alvark Tokyo v Utsunomiya Brex); the schedule_key column of bleague_schedule().

season

(integer optional): a guard, the season END year the game must belong to; a context whose Year differs raises hoopR_asset_fetch. NULL (default) = no check (the key alone selects the game).

Value

A hoopR_data tibble with these columns:

col_nametypedescription
schedule_keyintegerB.LEAGUE ScheduleKey (key space: B.LEAGUE games, ONE global integer sequence across B1, B2, B3 and every season). The {schedule_key} every game wrapper takes and the schedule page's list-item id.
seasonintegerSeason END year (2026 = 2025-26), the feed's Year (the START year) plus one.
feedcharacterSource feed of the row: v2 (v2_genius_contexts, B1/B2 from 2020-21) or v1 (v1_contexts: B3, B1/B2 2018-2020, and the 2016-17 / 2017-18 game-page embed). The feeds differ in id types, dates and some codes.
periodintegerPeriod number: 1-4 regulation; overtime numbering is unverified (no overtime sample).
event_nointegerEvent sequence number, ascending in game order. v2 counts in steps of 1000 (inserted corrections may fall in between); v1 counts 1, 2, 3...
action_codeintegerActionCD1, the primary action code: 1 / 2 3PT made / missed, 3 / 5 2PT outside the paint made / missed, 4 / 6 inside the paint, 7 / 8 free throw, 9 / 10 defensive / offensive rebound, 11 block, 12 assist, 13 turnover, 14 steal, 15 foul drawn, 16 and-one, 17 team turnover, 18 / 19 team rebounds (SWAPPED between feeds), 22-25 fouls, 80-85 game and clock events, 86 / 87 player in / out, 88 timeout, 89 substitution (v1).
actioncharacterEnglish slug for action_code (fg3_made, ft_missed, rebound_def, foul_personal, player_in, ...). The team-rebound codes 18 / 19 follow the feed column; null for a code no sample contains.
qualifier_code2integerActionCD2, a secondary qualifier (shot type, free throws awarded on a fouls, scoring context, 24 s violation); one code space shared with qualifier_code3. Null when the row has none.
qualifier2characterEnglish slug for qualifier_code2 (jump_shot, layup, dunk, free_throws_awarded_N, fast_break, second_chance, shooting_foul, ...); null when unknown.
qualifier_code3integerActionCD3, a tertiary qualifier (scoring context on made shots, shooting foul / foul-out on fouls); same code space as qualifier_code2.
qualifier3characterEnglish slug for qualifier_code3; null when unknown.
team_sidecharacterSide of the acting team from HomeAway (1 home, 2 away); null on game-level rows and official timeouts.
team_idcharacterB.LEAGUE TeamID as text (key space: B.LEAGUE clubs, stable across seasons AND club renames: 703 = Tochigi Brex in 2016-17 = Utsunomiya Brex in 2025-26). The feed sends a string on v2 and an integer on v1; both are text here. Not a player id.
team_name_jcharacterActing team name in Japanese; null on game-level rows and official timeouts.
player_idcharacterPrimary actor PlayerID as text (key space: B.LEAGUE persons). On a v1 substitution it is the player going out. Null on team rows and game-level rows.
player_nocharacterShirt number as text, so '00' and '0' stay distinct; null on team and game-level rows.
player_name_jcharacterPlayer name in Japanese (katakana for foreign players); null on team and game-level rows.
player2_idcharacterSecond actor PlayerID as text; on a v1 substitution the player coming in. v1 / embed only.
player2_nocharacterShirt number of the second actor (v1 / embed only).
player2_name_jcharacterSecond actor's name in Japanese (v1 / embed only).
rest_timecharacterGame clock REMAINING in the period as the feed's 'mm:ss' text (counts down from 10:00).
clock_secondsintegerGame clock remaining in the period in whole seconds (8:50 = 530), derived from rest_time.
scorecharacterRunning score 'home-away' after the event (e.g. '2-4'); null on player-in rows and v1 substitutions.
home_scoreintegerHome running score after the event, split from score.
away_scoreintegerAway running score after the event, split from score.
period_endlogicalTrue on the closing row of a period (ActionCD1 83).
game_endlogicalTrue on the game-end row on v1 and the embed; false on EVERY v2 row, the game-end row (81) included, so use action instead.
xnumericEvent x: percent (0-100) of the court LENGTH from the 'left' baseline (baskets near 5 and 95). Metres (x / 100 x 28) are an inference. 2022-23 onward on v2 only.
ynumericEvent y: percent (0-100) of the court WIDTH (baskets at 50). Which sideline is y = 0 is unverified; metres (y / 100 x 15) are an inference. 2022-23 onward on v2 only.
area_codeintegerShot-zone code 1-13 read from the site's shot-chart SVG: 1 restricted area, 2 rest of the paint, 3 / 7 baseline mid-range, 4 / 6 wing mid-range, 5 top-of-the-key mid-range, 8 / 12 corner 3, 9 / 11 wing 3, 10 top 3, 13 deep band. Of each pair the first is the side far along the baseline. Also set on turnover and foul rows; 2022-23 onward.
areacharacterEnglish zone slug for area_code (restricted_area, paint, baseline_mid_range, wing_mid_range, top_of_key_mid_range, corner_3, wing_3, top_3, deep_3); mirrored codes share a slug.
successlogicalOutcome flag: true = made / successful, false = missed; true on non-shot rows. v2 from 2022-23 only.
sidecharacterBasket the play is charted at: 'left' (x near 0) or 'right' (x near 100); flips at half-time. Present from 2025-26 only; earlier seasons leave it null and the end must be inferred from x.
play_textcharacterPlay description in Japanese: '#{shirt} {surname} {action} ({running count})'; a circle marks a make, a cross a miss, and an arrow a v1 substitution (out to in).
recorded_atPOSIXctWhen the event was logged, as a UTC instant (v2 stores UTC text, v1 a JST-offset .NET date, the embed epoch seconds).
edited_atPOSIXctWhen the event was last edited, as a UTC instant; null when never edited.
codeintegerFeed/organisation code repeated on every row: 546 on v2, 6 on v1; meaning unverified.

Details

The B.LEAGUE (Japan Professional Basketball League: B1, B2, B3) wrappers mirror sdv-py's sportsdataverse.basketball.bleague wrappers of the same names: same arguments, the same snake_case columns and types, one row per sdv-py row.

Unofficial and unsupported. The game contexts are JSON objects in B.LEAGUE's own public S3 bucket (b-league.s3.amazonaws.com, the store its game pages read), and the schedule, standings and game_detail pages of www.bleague.jp are parsed here. Neither host publishes terms for this use (the site's /terms/ answers 404; robots.txt sets a Crawl-delay only for msnbot and bingbot). Requests are spaced at least one second apart per host; 429 and 5xx answers are retried (three attempts). SportsDataverse has not ruled on the site's terms, so the data is not redistributed as release assets.

Seasons are END years (season = 2026 is 2025-26); the site's own Year / year= is the START year, so the request sends year = season - 1. Game wrappers take the global schedule_key (one integer sequence across B1, B2, B3 and every season: 1 = the 2016-17 opener, 5856 in 2020-21, 500017 in 2022-23, 504734 / 505508 B1 / B2 and 10693 B3 in 2025-26); list a day's keys with bleague_schedule().

Feeds. A game is read from the v2 feed (B1/B2 from 2020-21), else the v1 feed (B3 and B1/B2 2018-2020), else the game page's embedded copy (the only source of 2016-17 and 2017-18), decided at run time. v2 ids are strings, v1 ids integers: both become text here. v1 adds leaders and the score track; the team-rebound codes 18 / 19 are swapped between the feeds and a v1 substitution is one row where v2 has two. Player and team names are Japanese (English names only on the box score and header). Game wrappers serve FINISHED games only. Each game wrapper fetches the context itself (two requests): fetch once per game per wrapper you need.

Errors are classed conditions, never a warning plus an empty frame: hoopR_no_data (no source holds the game, a schedule day without games, HTTP 404), hoopR_bad_request (a non-integer or out-of-range argument, HTTP 400 / 422) and hoopR_asset_fetch (any other failure: another status, a transport error, a non-JSON or non-HTML body, an error or changed body, an unfinished game, a context or page for another game, season, tab or day, a truncated schedule list, or layout drift). All inherit hoopR_error.
